claim: LACIE calibrates verbalized confidence by casting it as preference optimization over a simulated speaker-listener game, where the reward is whether a listener model (not ground-truth correctness alone) accepts or rejects an answer based on how confident it sounds.
stance_target: an alternative, non-sampling-signal-based elicitation mechanism (pragmatics/listener-judgment rather than distilling the model's own sampling distribution)
quoted_support: we cast calibration as a preference optimization problem, creating data via a two-agent speaker-listener game, where a speaker model's outputs are judged by a simulated listener.

claim: LACIE produces an average 20.7-point AUROC gain and 7.8-point calibration-error decrease in induced listener calibration across three speaker models (Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B, Llama3-70B), plus an 18% absolute precision improvement.
stance_target: preference-optimization-based verbal confidence calibration achieves large discrimination gains at 7-70B scale
quoted_support: Using LACIE on three different speaker models (Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B, and Llama3-70B), we obtain substantial gains in induced listener calibration, with an average 20.7 point gain in AUROC over the base model and a 7.8 point decrease in calibration error.

claim: LACIE-trained models transfer benefits to human listeners: a 47% decrease in the rate at which humans accept incorrect answers, without significantly increasing rejection of correct answers.
stance_target: confidence-calibration gains measured against a simulated listener transfer to real human judgment
scope_conditions: human evaluation study on TriviaQA-trained LACIE model
quoted_support: a model trained with LACIE results in a 47% decrease in the rate of false answers being accepted without significantly increasing the rate of rejection for correct answers.

claim: LACIE calibration transfers across datasets: a model trained on TriviaQA and evaluated zero-shot on TruthfulQA shows a 28% absolute improvement in truthfulness metrics, and LACIE induces emergent abstention behavior ('I don't know') for likely-wrong answers without being explicitly trained to abstain.
stance_target: cross-dataset generalization and emergent secondary behavior from confidence-calibration training, paralleling the emergent self-verification finding in CSFT (2506.03723)
quoted_support: training leads to more hedging and abstention, as well as more detailed outputs and more authoritative tone when the model is actually correct... we train our models on TriviaQA and evaluate them on TruthfulQA... LACIE results in a 28% absolute improvement to truthfulness

claim: LACIE is not evaluated on any code-generation task; its evaluation is limited to TriviaQA (training) and TruthfulQA (transfer), both open-domain factual QA.
stance_target: domain gap: pragmatics/listener-based confidence calibration has not been validated on code LLMs
quoted_support: We use two datasets in this paper. First, for our finetuning experiments and human study, we use TriviaQA... The second dataset we use is TruthfulQA
